title: Window Frame Specifications: ROWS vs RANGE vs GROUPS
realWorldScenario: A financial risk officer needs a 3-day rolling sum of repayments per borrower to detect repayment surges. Because multiple repayments occur on the same day, using `ROWS BETWEEN` produces different totals depending on arbitrary row sorting.
questionStatement: Explain the difference between `ROWS`, `RANGE`, and `GROUPS` framing modes in SQL window functions. Write a query against `repayments` that calculates both a 2-row physical moving average (`ROWS`) and a calendar-date-based rolling 3-day sum (`RANGE`) per loan.
starterCode:
SELECT 
    id,
    loan_id,
    payment_date,
    amount,
    -- 2-row moving average (current row and 1 preceding physical row)
    AVG(amount) OVER (
        PARTITION BY loan_id 
        ORDER BY payment_date, id 
        ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS physical_2row_avg,
    -- Rolling sum over identical dates
    SUM(amount) OVER (
        PARTITION BY loan_id 
        ORDER BY amount
        RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS range_accum_sum
FROM repayments
ORDER BY loan_id, payment_date;
expectedConcepts: ROWS operates on physical row offsets
RANGE operates on logical value boundaries (peers lumped together)
GROUPS operates on peer rank clusters
Default window frame trap: RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
hints: Notice that if two rows have the same amount, RANGE treats them as tied peers.
ROWS treats every row distinctly based on physical sequence.
Check the default frame when ORDER BY is provided.

testCases.description: Verify ROWS physical average and RANGE cumulative calculations
testCases.setupSql:
CREATE TABLE repayments (id INT, loan_id INT, payment_date VARCHAR(10), amount NUMERIC);
INSERT INTO repayments VALUES (1, 101, '2026-01-01', 100), (2, 101, '2026-01-02', 200), (3, 101, '2026-01-03', 300);
testCases.expectedOutputSql: SELECT id, loan_id, payment_date, amount, AVG(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY loan_id ORDER BY payment_date, id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS physical_2row_avg, SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY loan_id ORDER BY amount RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS range_accum_sum FROM repayments ORDER BY loan_id, payment_date;
